To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) there exists a new concept called decisional second-preimage (DSP) resistance, and (2) DSP implies preimage (P) resistance.

(i) the gap between second-preimages and first-preimages for length-preserving functions is filled by a new concept called decisional second-preimage resistant (DSPR); (ii) the new concept is useful for multi-target preimage problems, which are important for hash-based signature schemes; and (iii) a tight reduction can be achieved for all length-preserving functions that are DSFR.
• Decisional second-preimage resistant functions are preimage resistant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: when does decisional second-preimage-resistance imply preimage-resistance?
the following question: when does second-preimage resistance imply preimage resistance?
the following question: when can a length-preserving hash function that is second-preimage resistant be preimage resistant?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a hash function that is decisional second-preimage resistant is also preimage resistant, and that a hash function is preimage resistant if and only if it is preimage resistant for a single target.
, in the random-oracle model, a length-preserving hash function is preimage-resistant if and only if it is second-preimage resistant.
the security of all length-presering hash-based signatures is equivalent to second preimage resistance, with no interactivity, and with a tight reduction.
